clue.text: Impromptu expression of dissatisfaction with shirt-maker?

definitions.meaning: said or done without preparation, ad lib
a grumble that the sleeve ends of a shirt are badly made: the wristbands are no good

explanation.surface: Someone spontaneously grumbles about the person who tailored their shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes OFF as 'not right', as food that has gone off, applied to the cuff the shirt-maker sewed.
explanation.definitionFit: Remarks made spontaneously, without notes, are described with this idiom.

clue.text: Grain vessels heading off

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for vessels is taken away, its head removed

parts.note: boats are vessels

explanation.surface: Ships carrying cereal set sail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading off' looks like ships leaving port; it removes B from BOATS.
explanation.definitionFit: Oats are a cereal crop, grown for their grain.

clue.text: Rage makes you pelt over yard

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits above, over, the second

parts.note: an animal's pelt is its fur

explanation.surface: Someone is so angry they throw things across the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pelt' reads as a verb, to throw things at, but it is the noun, an animal's coat.
explanation.definitionFit: Fury is violent anger, a synonym of rage.

clue.text: Man, one taking on charge presented by progenitor?

definitions.text: Man, one taking on charge presented by progenitor?

parts.note: HE is the pronoun for a man
I is the Roman numeral for one
a rap is a criminal charge, as in 'take the rap'
a progenitor is a parent or ancestor

explanation.surface: A man inherits a responsibility handed down by his father.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: the person who will take on the charge passed down by the reigning parent.
explanation.definitionFit: The heir apparent is the person whose right to succeed cannot be displaced, next in line to inherit.

clue.text: Family gathering's beginning with the sound of a bell

parts.note: a clan is an extended family

indicators.note: the beginning of the word gathering is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A family reunion starts when a bell rings.
explanation.definitionFit: A clang is a loud ringing metallic noise, such as a struck bell makes.

clue.text: Idiot made a meal of going round tee with putter, initially -driver should be seen here!

indicators.note: the word for idiot goes round, encloses, the next pieces

parts.note: a fool is an idiot
the letter T is spelt tee

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of putter

parts.note: to have made a meal of something is to have eaten it

explanation.surface: A golfer makes a fuss over teeing off, and a driver ought to be visible here.
explanation.walkthrough: Golf words (tee, putter, driver) mislead: the driver is a train driver.
explanation.definitionFit: The footplate is the platform in a steam locomotive cab where the driver and fireman stand.

clue.text: Introductions for books usually mean further paperwork

indicators.note: the introductions of the next four words are their opening letters

explanation.surface: Prefaces to books tend to generate yet more administrative documents.
explanation.walkthrough: BUMF is British slang for tedious paperwork or junk mail.
explanation.definitionFit: Bumf is slang for boring forms and documents, unwanted printed matter.

clue.text: Nude dancing, during which a small number quit flat

indicators.note: the following pieces go inside the anagram, during it
dancing moves the letters of nude about

parts.note: to leave is to quit
N stands for an unspecified number in maths

explanation.surface: A small group walk out of a naked dance performance, finding it dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' turns NUDE into UNED, and 'during which' puts LEAVE + N inside it. 'flat' is bread made without yeast.
explanation.definitionFit: Unleavened bread is baked without a raising agent, so it stays thin like a pancake.

clue.text: Struggle to embrace bird-it may be brothers in love!

indicators.note: the word for struggle wraps around, embraces, the next pieces

parts.note: a fray is a fight or struggle
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A fight breaks out over a bird, which might be siblings who care for each other.
explanation.definitionFit: Fraternity is brotherly feeling, the affection of brothers for one another.

clue.text: One who finishes trio meant for recomposition? Right

indicators.note: the letters of trio meant are composed again in a new order

explanation.surface: A composer finishes off a piece meant for three players by rewriting it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recomposition' suggests music for a trio, but it rearranges TRIOMEANT into TERMINATO.
explanation.definitionFit: A terminator brings things to an end, so is something that ends a process.

clue.text: Insect burrowing into leaf repeatedly?

indicators.note: an insect burrowing into the leaf churns its letters around

explanation.surface: A small bug keeps tunnelling into a leaf.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of LEAF, stirred up, give a parasite that lives on fur rather than leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: A flea is a small wingless jumping insect.

clue.text: It incorporates us in a more prominent case

definitions.text: It incorporates us in a more prominent case

parts.words: It incorporates us in a more prominent case
parts.note: written in upper case, the more prominent kind of letter, 'us' becomes the abbreviation for the United States; the answer is the continent that contains it

explanation.surface: Something takes us in, with a stronger legal argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' looks legal but means letter case: 'us' in capitals is US, the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: The continent includes the USA, Canada and Mexico.

clue.text: The most recent development in explosives technology?

definitions.text: The most recent development in explosives technology?

parts.words: The most recent development in explosives technology?
parts.note: the newest thing in bombs would be the latest bang; the phrase means fully modern

explanation.surface: A news item about the latest advances in bombs.
explanation.definitionFit: Something completely current or modern is described with this idiom.

clue.text: Shout about a boy dressing

indicators.note: the word for shout goes about, around, the other pieces

parts.note: to scream is to shout
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: Someone yells at a youngster getting dressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dressing' reads as putting clothes on, but it is a sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Salad cream is a British bottled condiment, like a tangy mayonnaise, put on salads.

clue.text: Opera: vital aria without one in error gets cheers

indicators.note: in error means the remaining letters are in a mistaken order
without means a letter is removed from vital aria

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
ta is British slang for thanks, like cheers

explanation.surface: An important aria from an opera is sung wrongly but still gets applause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without one' removes an I from VITALARIA, leaving VTALARA, which 'in error' rearranges to LATRAVIA.
explanation.definitionFit: La Traviata is Verdi's opera about the courtesan Violetta.

clue.text: Mostly lack appeal in performance, like unaccompanied choirs

indicators.note: in performance means the letters are put on show in a new arrangement
mostly means the word lack loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A choir's show lacks charm, as unaccompanied singing sometimes does.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' drops the K from 'lack' to leave LAC, and 'in performance' rearranges LAC + APPEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A cappella singing is performed by voices alone, without instruments.

clue.text: Fellow due to tangle with a girl in difficulties?

definitions.text: Fellow due to tangle with a girl in difficulties?

indicators.note: in difficulties means the letters are in trouble and thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A man is about to get involved with a woman in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a beach guard is the fellow bound to grapple with a swimmer in difficulties.
explanation.definitionFit: A lifeguard is employed to rescue swimmers who get into trouble.

clue.text: Something linked with TV show that is presented in a can

indicators.note: the abbreviation for that is is presented inside the word for a can

parts.note: a tin is a can
ie is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A television programme is presented in a tin.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie-in is merchandise or a book connected with a film or TV programme.

clue.text: Unusual type of horse runs to river

indicators.note: the letter for runs is added to the river's name

parts.note: the Aire is a river in Yorkshire
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A rare breed of horse gallops down to the river.
explanation.walkthrough: The horse is a clothes horse, a frame for drying laundry; the Aire is a river in Yorkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: An airer is a frame for drying clothes, also called a clothes horse.

clue.text: One who's not constrained about each amount of information found in newspaper

indicators.note: the pieces are found inside the newspaper's abbreviation

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times, a newspaper
re means about, concerning
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A free-spirited journalist finds information in the paper about everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is British slang for information, as in 'get the gen'.
explanation.definitionFit: A free agent acts independently, bound by no contract or obligation.

clue.text: Fruit and vegetables used to be supplied by this stage

definitions.text: Fruit and vegetables used to be supplied by this stage

parts.words: Fruit and vegetables used to be supplied by this stage
parts.note: a London district that housed the famous produce market until 1974 and is now known for its opera house stage

explanation.surface: Produce was once delivered from a particular theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: The grid prints COVENIGARDEN; the London place is COVENT GARDEN, home of the old fruit and vegetable market and of the Royal Opera House.
explanation.definitionFit: The London district hosted the produce market and now the Royal Opera House.

clue.text: True, millions can be found in country

parts.note: real means true, genuine

explanation.surface: It's true that millions live in this land.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a kingdom, a country ruled by a monarch.

clue.text: Speech defect is evident in recording

indicators.note: the word is is evident inside the recording's abbreviation

parts.note: an LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: A speech problem is obvious on a tape.
explanation.definitionFit: A lisp is a speech impediment turning S sounds into TH.

clue.text: Unpleasant look of headless goblin

indicators.note: headless means the word for goblin loses its first letter

parts.note: a bogle is a goblin or bogey in Scottish and northern folklore

explanation.surface: A goblin without a head gives a nasty stare.
explanation.walkthrough: BOGLE is a Scottish word for a goblin or ghost.
explanation.definitionFit: To ogle is to stare lecherously, an unpleasant leering look.

clue.text: Former partner's in the morning paper

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
am stands for ante meridiem, in the morning

explanation.surface: An ex-partner appears in the morning newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'paper' looks like a newspaper but is a test paper.
explanation.definitionFit: An examination paper is a written test.

clue.text: Grass mostly waiting to implicate one not acting illegally

indicators.note: mostly means the word for grass loses its final letter

parts.note: a lawn is an area of grass
a is one, the indefinite article
biding is waiting, as in biding one's time

explanation.surface: An informer hangs around waiting to incriminate someone who has done nothing wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' reads as an informer, but it is LAWN, losing its end.
explanation.definitionFit: A law-abiding citizen keeps to the rules and commits no crimes.

clue.text: Repast that finally is extracted from tin?

indicators.note: the letter is taken out of the word for tin

parts.note: tin is an example of a metal

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of that

explanation.surface: A meal is eaten straight from the can.
explanation.walkthrough: Tin is an example of METAL, hence the question mark; take out T, the end of 'that'.
explanation.definitionFit: A meal is a repast, an occasion of eating food.

clue.text: Unhappy sad male swallowing a very soft lump in the throat?

indicators.note: the anagram swallows, takes inside it, the other pieces
unhappy means the letters of sad male are in a disturbed state

parts.note: pp is pianissimo, the musical marking for very soft

explanation.surface: A miserable man gulps down something soft and feels choked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unhappy' rearranges SADMALE to ADAMSLE, which 'swallowing' opens to take in A + PP. A 'lump in the throat' is usually emotion, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The Adam's apple is the projection of the larynx at the front of the neck.
